ruleName: Out of bounds and provisional ball
title: When is a ball out of bounds?
question: Which of these situations means your ball is out of bounds?

choices.text: The entire ball is over the line made by the out of bounds posts.
Part of the ball is still on the course side of the line marked by the out of bounds posts.
The ball is touching an out of bounds post but most of it is still on the course side.

explanation: A ball is only out of bounds if its entire location is over the line defined by the out of bounds (white) posts. If any part of the ball is in bounds, it is not out of bounds.

juniorVersion.title: How do you know if your golf ball is out of bounds?
juniorVersion.question: When is your golf ball really out of bounds?

choices.text: When your whole ball is past the line made by the out of bounds posts.
When part of your ball is still on the golf course side of the line made by the out of bounds posts.
When your ball is touching an out of bounds post but most of it is still on the golf course side.

juniorVersion.explanation: Your ball is only out of bounds if the whole ball is over the line made by the out of bounds posts. If any part of your ball is on or inside the line, your ball is still in play.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The area outside the golf course that you are not allowed to play from.
White sticks in the ground used to show where out of bounds starts.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Show the children a line between two white posts and place balls in different spots to demonstrate which ones are out and which are in bounds.
likelyMisconceptions: Thinking the ball is out of bounds if it touches the line or a post.
Thinking the ball is out if any small part is over the line, when actually the whole ball has to be over the line.
